To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
PLEST is a program that can generate estimates for the area of standard-cell layouts that are within 10% (on average) of the measured area of the layout.
PLEST can be used to estimate the area of VLSI integrated circuits with reasonable accuracy and that the program can serve as a basis for a register-transfer level area estimator.
the area of a VLSI integrated circuit can be estimated with a 10% error by a program based on a probabilistc model for placement.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of an area estimation system that is applicable at the register-transfer level and that will be capable of estimating the area consumption of the layout for a given design.
the estimation of area consumption for VLSI chips, from the register-transfer design level to the physical design level.
the development of a methodology for area estimation that can be integrated into the design cycle.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
PLEST has been shown to be a useful tool in the design of VLSI circuits.
the PLEST algorithm is capable of producing a range of estimates which are within 10% for the measured area of six chips.
, in the case of the six chips studied, the estimated area was within 10% (on the high side) of the measured area.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, in general, it is possible to estimate the area of VLSI integrated circuits to within 10% with the use of a simple probabilistic placement model.
, in the absence of any other information, the estimated area consumption for a design can be within 10-20% of the actual area consumption.
the ARREST system is a useful tool for estimating the chip area of a standard cell layout.
The main takeaway from our work is that
probabilistic placement models can be used for estimating chip area.
a probabilistic placement model can be used as the basis for estimating chip area consumption.
the probabilistic approach to estimating layout area is a viable alternative to the deterministic approach.
